skill.name: code-patterns
skill.description: Reference guide for common TypeScript code patterns, including design patterns, error handling, async control, and data access.
skill.summary: Find practical TypeScript patterns for common software design problems.

security_audit.summary: Static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md. They are false positives from Markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, interface names, and database examples. No evidence found for prompt injection, command execution, real database access, or reconnaissance behavior.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples can trigger simplistic static patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Keep code fences labeled as TypeScript and state that snippets are documentation examples only.

static_findings.snippet: pay(amount: number) { console.log(`Paid ${amount} via credit card`); }
return this.db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', [id]);

content.value_statement: Developers often need a quick reminder of common implementation patterns. This skill provides concise TypeScript examples for design, async, error handling, and data access patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows examples for Factory, Builder, Singleton, Adapter, Decorator, Strategy, and Observer patterns.
Summarizes when each pattern fits a common programming problem.
Includes TypeScript snippets for Result types, retry logic, queues, and debounce utilities.
Provides data access examples for repository and unit of work patterns.
Helps compare pattern choices during refactoring and design discussions.
limitations: Examples are short references and are not complete production modules.
The skill does not validate generated code or run tests.
Database examples omit schema design, connection handling, and migrations.
Security controls must be added for real application code.

use_cases.title: Choose a data access pattern
use_cases.description: Compare repository and unit of work patterns before refactoring service persistence code.

use_cases.title: Structure event behavior
use_cases.description: Use debounce, observer, or strategy examples to organize UI events and runtime choices.

use_cases.title: Standardize review language
use_cases.description: Reference pattern names and tradeoffs during design reviews and onboarding.

prompt_templates.title: Find a pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to solve [problem]. Use this skill to suggest one matching pattern and explain why it fits.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [pattern A] and [pattern B] for [context]. Recommend which one to use and list tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor existing code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for pattern opportunities. Suggest small TypeScript refactors using patterns from this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Design module architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript module for [feature]. Select appropriate patterns from this skill and explain integration boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need to choose between Strategy and Factory for payments.
output_examples.output: Use Strategy when payment behavior changes at runtime. Use Factory when creating payment objects from a type or configuration.

output_examples.input: My API calls sometimes fail temporarily.
output_examples.output: The skill points to retry with backoff. Limit attempts and pair retries with clear error handling.

output_examples.input: I want to hide database logic from business services.
output_examples.output: Use Repository for data access abstraction. Add Unit of Work only when multiple writes need one transaction.

best_practices: Treat examples as starting points and adapt names, types, and error handling to your project.
Ask for pattern tradeoffs before asking for implementation details.
Pair generated code with tests, linting, and security review.
anti_patterns: Do not force a design pattern into simple code that already reads clearly.
Do not copy database examples without adding validation, authorization, and transaction safety.
Do not treat concise snippets as complete application architecture.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference patterns that can guide implementation and review.

faq.question: Is it limited to TypeScript?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript, but the ideas can transfer to other languages.

faq.question: Can it choose the best pattern for my feature?
faq.answer: It can suggest options when you provide requirements, constraints, and code context.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Only general coding structure is included. Security requirements must be reviewed separately.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are the snippets production ready?
faq.answer: No. They need validation, tests, logging, and project-specific integration.
